Dear Mohammad,

 

Yesterday I’ve mailed you concerning our preparations for our big upcoming study. I came across some other issues that I hope you could help me with.

Disable the “previous” button:

In the surveys participants can navigate with a “previous” and “next” button (or whatever the original English translation is). For a specific questionnaire we don’t want participants to navigate back so that they cannot change their answer and end in another branched arm of the survey. Thus we want them to choose between A & B and not click on B look at it and go back and choose A and look at that. In the questionnaire settings and “Avicenna learn” I haven’t found any explanation about such an option, but assume that this is such a simple feature that you must have this for sure. Is it thus possible to disable the “previous” button?

Display pictures in questionnaires (Apple):

I have added some pictures to a questionnaire (study: 4080, survey: 22785). While I saw this picture on my phone (Android, Samsung), my colleague did not (IPhone). See screenshots attached.

Could it be that there is a technical problem with IPhones or are only some picture formats supported by iOS? Do you know about this problem?

Line breaks in data exports:

Yesterday I tried to export the data (study 4080). I had difficulties opening the csv files properly. My analysis software (RStudio) gave the error message “more columns than column names”. Especially when inspecting the data files in the “old format”, I saw that there were line breaks in columnames when there was a line break in the item, which makes all the following column names the first data row (if you understand what I mean). I do not wish to remove all line breaks in the surveys as these are really useful to improve readability. I am wondering if the problem occurs at my end (when uploading the data) or that this is a “mistake” in the exporting function. That is, that when exporting it does not take the label (without line break) to make a column name, but the item itself.

Thanks, Mohammad, for looking into this. I hope that for all the issues there is a quick fix that I have just overlooked.

All the best,

Anne

Hi Anne
Thanks for adding me to the project, I'll look into the issue.
In the meantime, please use one of the following methods to remove all the line breaks. If it didn't help, please let me know:

Method 1: Using Microsoft Excel
  1. Open Excel and press ALT + F11 to open the Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) editor.
  2. Go to Insert > Module to insert a new module.
  3. Copy and paste the following code into the module:
Sub RemoveLineBreaks() Dim ws As Worksheet Dim cell As Range Dim firstRow As Range ' Assuming the active sheet is the one with your data Set ws = ThisWorkbook.ActiveSheet ' Get the first row of the active sheet Set firstRow = ws.Rows(1) ' Loop through each cell in the first row For Each cell In firstRow.Cells ' Remove line breaks: vbLf is for line feed (LF), vbCr is for carriage return (CR) cell.Value = Application.WorksheetFunction.Substitute(cell.Value, vbLf, "") cell.Value = Application.WorksheetFunction.Substitute(cell.Value, vbCr, "") Next cell End Sub
  1. Close the VBA editor and go back to your Excel worksheet.
  2. Run the macro by pressing ALT + F8, select RemoveLineBreaks, and click Run.

This macro scans each cell in the first row of your active worksheet and removes line breaks, which are typically represented by vbLf (line feed) and vbCr (carriage return). Make sure to replace these special characters with an empty string to effectively remove them.


Method 2: Using Google Sheets:

  1. Open your Google Sheets document.
  2. Click on Extensions in the menu.
  3. Select Apps Script to open the script editor.
    1. Delete any code in the script editor and replace it with the following code:
    JavaScript
    function removeLineBreaks() { var sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet().getActiveSheet(); // Get the first row var firstRow = sheet.getRange(1, 1, 1, sheet.getLastColumn()); var data = firstRow.getValues(); // Loop through each cell in the first row for (var i = 0; i < data[0].length; i++) { if (typeof data[0][i] === 'string') { // Remove line breaks: "\n" is the line feed character data[0][i] = data[0][i].replace(/\n/g, ''); } } // Set the modified data back to the first row firstRow.setValues(data); }
  1. Click the disk icon or press Ctrl + S to save the script, and give your project a name if prompted.
  2. Close the Apps Script editor.
  3. Back in your Google Sheets, you can run the script by going to Extensions > Apps Script, then clicking the play (▶) button to run the removeLineBreaks function.

Always ensure your Google Sheets file is backed up before running scripts that modify data.
